conduct: The user leads search for the catalogue and named this topic a moment ago because of what they see in the query logs. Shoppers type three kinds of thing into the one search box: a brand name on its own — about a third of all queries — which today lands on a keyword results page instead of the brand's page; a product with a constraint, like 'red dress under 50', where the colour and the price are matched as plain keywords and the constraint is ignored; and how-to questions like 'how to wash wool', which return products when the care guides would answer them. They want search to tell these apart before it answers. Their constraints: catalogue search runs on Elasticsearch, two engineers own search part-time, and there is no model-serving infrastructure — anything that needs a hosted model is out for this release. They answer each question in a sentence or two, in their own words, and they do not know which files parse queries — they say so rather than guess.
